replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering key functionalities such as report submission, status viewing, notifications, statistics access, administrative tasks, and external maintenance workflows. However, there is a notable omission regarding the anonymous reporting feature mentioned in the software description (Section A), which is not reflected in any low-level goal. Additionally, the "Support External Chatbot for Citizen Updates" low-level goal introduces functionality that was not explicitly described in the high-level goals or the software description, potentially leading to inconsistency.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

Rewrite the original goal to emphasize these structured stages and ensure it aligns with the documented process.

decisions.rationale: The original goal 'Ensure Efficient Report Approval and Assignment' is NOT_EQUIVALENT to its prime, but the prime provides a more detailed and documented workflow for report lifecycle management. The original goal should be rewritten to reflect the structured stages of approval, rejection, suspension, resolution, and mandatory feedback.
The goal 'Assign Reports to External Maintenance Personnel Based on Category' is fully documented, covering the assignment process and workflow for external maintenance personnel.
The goal 'Enable External Maintenance Personnel to Manage Assigned Reports' is fully documented, including secure communication channels and status updates.

The goal 'Enable Citizen Reporting of Urban Issues' is fully documented and supported by the project description. It allows registered citizens to submit reports with location, description, category, and mandatory photo attachment via the web interface.

The goal 'Enable Citizen Viewing of Report Status' is fully documented and supported by the project description. It allows citizens to view the current status of submitted reports via the dashboard and interactive map.

The goal 'Provide Real-Time Notifications and Email Updates' is fully documented and supported by the project description. It ensures citizens receive timely platform notifications and emails about report status changes and messages from municipal staff.

The goal 'Support Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics' is fully documented and supported by the project description. It allows non-registered users to view public statistics on report trends and categories to promote awareness and data-driven urban planning.

The goal 'Enable Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making' is fully documented and supported by the project description. It provides municipal administrators with private access to detailed statistics and system configuration tools for managing external company access and optimizing resource allocation.

The goal 'Ensure Efficient Report Approval and Assignment' is fully documented and supported by the project description. It provides a structured workflow for reports to move through approval, assignment, and resolution stages with clear state transitions and accountability.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are well-defined, functional, and align with the high-level goals. They cover all necessary actions for each actor without any contradictions or omissions. However, there is a minor issue: the low-level goal "Citizen views report status via dashboard" is redundant because it is already covered by "Citizen receives notification of report status change," which implies real-time visibility. Additionally, while not strictly an error, the system description mentions that rejected reports require a written explanation from the Organization Office, but this is not explicitly included in the low-level goals.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are well-defined, functional, and align with the high-level goals. They cover all necessary actions for each actor without any contradictions or omissions. However, there is a minor issue: the high-level goal "Allow Citizens to View Report Status via Dashboard" does not explicitly mention the ability for citizens to follow other citizens' open reports, which is described in the software description under "CITIZEN UPDATES." This functionality should be included as a low-level goal for the Citizen actor.

decisions.rationale: The goal 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location, Description, Category, and Photos' is fully documented in the project description under section A (Reports). The HLG prime matches the described functionality without gaps.

The goal 'Allow Citizens to View Report Status via Dashboard' is documented in the project description under section C (Citizen Updates). The HLG prime accurately reflects the described functionality.

The goal 'Provide Real-Time Notifications and Email Updates for Citizen Reports' is fully documented in section C (Citizen Updates). The HLG prime aligns with the described features, including email notification options.
The goal 'Enable Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics' is documented in section D (Statistics). The HLG prime matches the described public statistics functionality without deviations.

The goal 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making' is documented for the Municipal Administrator actor. The HLG prime accurately reflects the described administrative capabilities.
The goal 'Enable Organization Office Staff to Review and Approve Reports' is documented in section B (Report Lifecycle). The HLG prime matches the described review and approval process.

The goal 'Enable Technical Office Staff to Assign and Manage Reports by Category' is documented in section B (Report Lifecycle). The HLG prime aligns with the described assignment and management process.

The goal 'Support External Maintenance Personnel in Managing Assigned Reports' is documented in section B (Report Lifecycle). The HLG prime matches the described functionality for external maintenance personnel.

The goal 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location, Description, Category, and Photos' is fully documented in the project description. It aligns with citizens submitting reports including location coordinates, a title and textual description, selecting a predefined category, and uploading mandatory photos (up to 3).

The goal 'Allow Citizens to View Report Status via Dashboard' is well-documented. It describes providing citizens with a dashboard to view the current status of their submitted reports, including transitions through various states.

The goal 'Provide Real-Time Notifications and Email Updates for Citizen Reports' is fully documented. It ensures citizens receive timely platform notifications and emails regarding state changes and communications related to their reports, with the option to disable email notifications in user settings.

The goal 'Enable Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics' is documented. It allows non-registered users to view public statistics on report trends and categories, including maps and summary tables filtered by category, status, or date.

The goal 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making' is well-documented. It provides municipal administrators with private access to detailed statistics, system configuration tools, and controls to manage external company access and optimize resource allocation.

The goal 'Enable Organization Office Staff to Review and Approve Reports' is fully documented. It allows Organization Office Staff to review citizen reports and mark them as accepted or rejected, with mandatory written explanations for rejected reports.

The goal 'Enable Technical Office Staff to Assign and Manage Reports by Category' is documented. It allows Technical Office Staff to assign approved reports to the appropriate technical office based on category, update statuses, and manage transitions through the report lifecycle.

The goal 'Support External Maintenance Personnel in Managing Assigned Reports' is well-documented. It allows external maintenance personnel to access and update reports assigned to them, including marking reports as In Progress or Resolved, with internal communication channels visible only to staff and external workers.
The goal of submitting reports with location, description, category, and photos is fully documented in Section A.
Citizens viewing report status via a dashboard is supported by the notification and visibility rules in Section C.
Platform notifications and emails for state changes are explicitly documented in Section C.

Remove the reference to maps and summary tables for public statistics, as these are only documented for the portal view of reports, not the statistics section.
